assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect opened a new class of electronic phases classified by band topology rather than symmetry breaking. The theoretical prediction, the HgTe/CdTe observation of edge transport and the three-dimensional extensions have reshaped how electronic structure is understood and computed. As a materials theorist I value that the concept translated directly into material-specific predictions that experiment confirmed.
assessment.attribution: The Kane-Mele Z2 classification is decisive on the theory side and Molenkamp's group delivered the experimental realisation after the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. The supplied names support a theory-plus-experiment configuration, but the contribution of the BHZ prediction and of early three-dimensional work is not represented in the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many independent groups and material families over nearly two decades, with a stable interpretation and a large follow-on literature, so recognition is timely and not premature.
uncertainties: Credit for the HgTe prediction (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang) is outside the supplied names and may complicate a fair configuration.
Whether the three-dimensional topological insulator discoveries should be recognised together with the quantum spin Hall effect is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock combines magic-wavelength trapping with many-atom interrogation and now reaches fractional uncertainties near 1e-18. It underpins searches for variation of constants, relativistic geodesy and a possible redefinition of the second, so the impact on fundamental metrology is large and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice idea and demonstrated early strontium clocks; Ye's group drove the performance to the best accuracies and stability. Two laureates form a clean, defensible configuration, though the single-ion clock tradition and others also shaped the field.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent labs have reproduced lattice-clock performance at the 1e-18 level and comparisons across continents are routine. The maturity is high and the concept is well established.
uncertainties: The Nobel-recognised 2005 and 2012 prizes in related areas make some committee members weigh overlap with prior frequency-comb and ion-control awards.
A possible third contributor to the lattice-clock concept is not in the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Trapped-ion quantum logic established that a scalable quantum computer architecture was physically credible: the Cirac-Zoller gate proposal, the experimental demonstration of entangling gates and multi-qubit algorithms, and error-corrected operations. It is a foundational pillar of quantum information experiment and complements earlier recognition of ion control.
assessment.attribution: The Cirac-Zoller proposal supplies the theory, and Blatt's group executed the first controlled-NOT gate and large entangled states in Innsbruck. A theory-plus-experiment trio is natural, but other ion groups (NIST, Oxford, Maryland) have strong claims.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by many groups and now commercial platforms, though the final computational value of the approach remains open. Recognition is timely, with the topic having been sharpened by the 2012 and 2025 prizes in neighbouring areas.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize (Wineland, Haroche) may raise doubts about novelty of recognising ion control again.
The contribution of other experimental groups to ion-trap logic is not captured in the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle and the discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in twisted bilayer graphene created the moire-materials field. It is a striking case where electronic-structure theory anticipated an experimental landscape, and it has unified work on correlated physics in two-dimensional systems.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the continuum-model prediction and Jarillo-Herrero's group delivered the experimental discovery of the correlated and superconducting states. The three supplied names form a clean theory-and-experiment configuration; other experimental groups also contributed rapidly.
assessment.maturity: The discovery dates from 2018 and has been broadly reproduced, but the superconducting mechanism remains unsettled and the field is still developing. Recognition may be slightly early but the core finding is robust.
uncertainties: The origin of superconductivity in twisted bilayers remains debated.
The role of other early experimental groups and of substrate effects, including hBN encapsulation, is not resolved by the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental discovery of the Higgs boson verified the mechanism that gives mass to gauge bosons, completing the Standard Model's particle content. The measurement of couplings continues to constrain physics beyond the Standard Model. Its scientific importance is exceptional, though the 2013 prize recognised the theory.
assessment.attribution: The discovery was a very large collaborative effort. Founding leaders of ATLAS and CMS (Jenni, Della Negra, Virdee) are plausible representatives, but the supplied names include Gianotti as spokesperson at the time of discovery; any selection of three will be contested and compresses the efforts of thousands.
assessment.maturity: The discovery was independently confirmed by two experiments with a stable interpretation, so maturity is high. The rule of three and the existing prize for theory complicate timing.
uncertainties: Attribution inside a large collaboration is inherently difficult and the Nobel statutes constrain the choice of names.
Whether experimental credit is still prize-worthy after the 2013 prize is a matter of committee judgement.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory gave the first controllable non-perturbative framework for strongly correlated electrons, capturing the Mott transition and enabling realistic material calculations when combined with density functional theory. It has major impact on correlated materials, including transition-metal oxides and heavy fermions.
assessment.attribution: Metzner-Vollhardt introduced the infinite-dimensional limit, Georges-Kotliar formulated the mapping to the impurity problem, and others (Rozenberg, Jarrell, Müller-Hartmann) contributed. The supplied names are plausible but the credit is spread, and the allocation is genuinely disputed.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with thirty years of broad application, although the approximation is not exact in finite dimensions. I note my own working familiarity with the method, so I rank it conservatively relative to its prominence in my field.
uncertainties: Credit allocation among Metzner, Vollhardt, Georges, Kotliar and others is unresolved.
The approximation's quantitative reliability for realistic materials is still debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultrasoft pseudopotentials and the projector augmented-wave method made plane-wave first-principles calculations efficient and accurate for transition metals and oxides, and thereby enabled much of modern computational materials physics. Its use is vast across condensed matter and chemistry, though its character is methodological rather than a discovery of a new phenomenon.
assessment.attribution: Vanderbilt introduced ultrasoft pseudopotentials, Blöchl formulated PAW, and Kresse and collaborators implemented it in widely used codes and reconciled the two approaches. The supplied names are reasonable, though the history of pseudopotential development is broader.
assessment.maturity: Extremely mature and independently validated, including in multi-code reproducibility studies. The timing is not an issue, but the 1998 prize for density functional theory already recognised the foundation and the committee may judge the tools as secondary.
uncertainties: Whether a computational method fits the prize remit in physics is a committee judgement.
Many other developers of pseudopotentials and electronic-structure codes could claim credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The IceCube observation of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos and the later association with the blazar TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane opened neutrino astronomy at TeV-PeV energies and addressed cosmic-ray origins.
assessment.attribution: Halzen led the concept and the project and Karle was a principal figure in the construction and analysis. The collaboration is large, and the supplied names omit some leaders and early detectors such as AMANDA contributors.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is statistically well established and the source identification is evolving. Independent confirmation from KM3NeT and Baikal is growing but incomplete, so the field is in a developing state.
uncertainties: Credit for earlier neutrino-telescope developments such as AMANDA and DUMAND is unresolved.
